objective: Build the most useful source-transparent Isle Royale planning map in the Chris Izworski tool network without pretending static cartography is authoritative GIS.

D.name: decisionUtility
D.question: Can a visitor make a better access, hiking, camping, boating or orientation decision?

T.name: dataTruthCoverage
T.question: Are important layers present with authority/vintage/uncertainty represented honestly?

U.name: mapUsability
U.question: Can users search, filter, inspect, zoom and recover without fighting the interface?

P.name: provenanceFreshness
P.question: Can users tell where a feature came from, when it was updated, and whether it is current/reference/derived?

R.name: reliabilityPerformance
R.question: Does the tool fail soft, avoid API keys, and remain useful when a remote layer fails?

A.name: accessibility
A.question: Is core information reachable by keyboard and through a non-map feature list?

S.name: searchDiscovery
S.question: Does the canonical page answer the Isle Royale map intent with strong entity/schema/discovery signals?

N.name: networkFit
N.question: Does this connect cleanly to the existing Michigan/Great Lakes tool journey without cannibalization?

benchmark.target: All 16 NPMaps product families remain explicitly accounted for in the source manifest, with preferred upstream authority and a crawlable source desk/raw catalog link.
Runtime visitor web-map ingestion supports trails, camps, routes and POIs without a commercial map key.

The primary surface is a trip planner, not a GIS showcase: route planner before feature browsing; every route stop shows leg and cumulative distance; deletion is obvious from both stop list and route-marker popup; primary map controls expose only decision-useful layers (trails, camps, visitor/dock places, water/transport, maritime history, quiet/no-wake, relief). Original research-only science families remain provenance-cataloged but absent from planning controls. Undo/Redo must be action-aware: capture committed route state before each edit, restore geometry + mode + speed + hours/day + departure + Build/Explore state, label the next undo/redo action, dedupe no-op snapshots, and make compound campsite/day-end actions one history step. For paddle/motorboat mode, mileage is only valid after a zero-mapped-shoreline-crossing route resolves; each selected leg must be labeled on-map with its resolved water miles, and no straight fallback line may be drawn when water routing fails.
Every live/derived layer exposes source and status; science layers expose dataset vintage.
No NPS Park Tiles reuse, no navigation claim, no unlabeled manually-derived geometry, regulation-sensitive layers point to current NPS.
The map still loads a basemap, source catalog and fallback anchors if ArcGIS/OpenStreetMap supplementary services fail.
Keyboard controls, visible focus, status region and feature-list alternative are present.
Canonical, title/meta limits, Person node, WebApplication/Dataset schema and dateModified pass repo rules.
At least three contextual links into relevant existing tools or authority surfaces.
Geology, vegetation, historic raster and boating-zone layers have explicit ETL/publication paths rather than fake client-side pins.

hardGates: Do not use or hotlink NPS Park Tiles as the public basemap.
Do not present the map as a navigation chart or replacement for official NPS information.
Do not label approximate/manual fallback geometry as authoritative NPS GIS.
Do not expose newly discovered sensitive cultural/natural-resource coordinates automatically.
Do not ship a current-regulation layer without current NPS provenance.
Do not create a second canonical page for the same Isle Royale interactive-map intent.
Do not remove or silently substitute any of the 16 NPMaps completeness records.
Do not hide the entire source catalog behind JavaScript; preserve crawlable source rows and a raw catalog link.
Do not claim the measurement plan is complete unless all five privacy-safe Isle Royale product events are wired.
Do not call water routing smart if it is only a draggable straight-line sketch; water intelligence requires mapped-coastline avoidance plus route exposure/regulation/refuge analysis.

Do not call a multi-day water itinerary complete unless overnight recommendations require a current NPS Boat-In campground record, exclude current closure signals, and explicitly show a gap instead of inventing a campsite when no qualified stop fits the travel day.

Do not call scenario planning complete unless conservative, balanced, and ambitious plans are structurally distinct, applying a scenario preserves manual route points, source-backed overnight-stop truth gates remain intact, and scenario weather uses explicit itinerary target times across overnight layovers.

Do not call map-first routing complete if Build mode auto-exits after two points, map clicks scroll the user away from the map, campground clicks do not become explicit route stops, or map-selected NPS Boat-In camps can be silently replaced by scenario generation.

Do not call day-end planning complete unless users can explicitly set and clear campsite day ends from the route-building experience, those anchors override automatic day splitting across all scenarios, trip starts cannot become day ends, and water-trip day ends remain constrained by current NPS Boat-In/closure truth.

Do not call the route planner usable if the map remains reference-sized during Build mode, landscape tablet planning is constrained to a short viewport, full-map focus is unavailable, or Leaflet is not invalidated after responsive/focus layout changes.

Do not call Focus map complete if users must leave it to edit the trip, if its controls can drift from the side panel, or if Undo only deletes the last point instead of restoring full route-edit state with Redo support.

Do not call trip handoff complete if saving uploads route state, sharing puts route data in the server-visible query string, restored trips trust stale closure/Boat-In flags, or GPX can export a temporary straight fallback before trail/water routing resolves.

Do not call the planning surface usable if vegetation/change/fire controls reappear, if route stops lack leg+cumulative miles, if stop deletion depends on a tiny or hidden control, or if route planning is visually subordinate to feature browsing/prose.

Do not call Undo usable if speed/day/departure changes snapshot post-change DOM values, one click creates multiple history steps, no-op edits consume Undo, or the buttons cannot tell the user what action will be undone/redone.

Do not call water routing complete if route simplification can shortcut across coastline, selected on-land endpoints are drawn into the water route, failed water routing falls back to a straight line, or mileage is shown before a zero-crossing route resolves.
